content.title: Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex
content.text: The Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex (KSCVC) is a tourist attraction in Cape Canaveral offering exhibits, shows, and tours that showcase the history and future of NASA’s space program. The visitor’s center is located next to the famous Launch Complex 39, where operations for the Apollo, Skylab, and Space Shuttle programs were carried out. It’s also adjacent to the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station. The KSCVC has undergone major enhancements in recent years, including the implementation of LED video technology by SNA Displays to improve visitor experience. The most notable of those upgrades is the Kennedy Entry Experience, but others include large LED kiosks and the NASA Trailblazers exhibit. SNA Displays is the exclusive sponsor of the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex Entry Experience. Kennedy Entry Experience The Kennedy Entry Experience is a 3,000-square-foot LED spectacular situated at the entrance area of the KSCVC. Visitors are able to walk up to the massive ground-level display, which stands at 30 feet tall and extends 98 feet wide. The Entry Experience is designed to stimulate interest in space exploration and tell the story of NASA: past, present, and future. It frequently runs a six-minute animation with stunning 3D and forced-perspective content. The freestanding screen was built with EMPIRE™ Exterior LED display technology and employs a 6.6 mm pixel pitch. The Kennedy Entry Experience has a resolution of 1,368 x 4,464 and contains more than 6.1 million pixels. Designed with a smooth, seamless curve with a tight five-foot radius, it’s optimally designed for anamorphic content, which can create astounding 3D illusions from a specific vantage point. In addition to immersive themed content, the visitor complex will show live-input video of launches and other events as well as various event messaging.
